query: What is the difference between ionic and covalent bonding?
title: Ionic vs Covalent Bonding: The Essential Differences

scenes.title: Two Paths to Chemical Unity
scenes.narration: Chemical bonds form either by completely transferring electrons or by sharing them between partner atoms.
scenes.key_takeaway: Atoms bond through either electron transfer (ionic) or electron sharing (covalent).

scenes.title: Ionic Bonding: Complete Transfer
scenes.narration: In ionic bonding, metals transfer electrons to nonmetals, forming oppositely charged ions in rigid crystalline lattices.
scenes.key_takeaway: Metals donate electrons to nonmetals, forming electrostatic ionic lattices.

scenes.title: Covalent Bonding: Mutual Orbital Sharing
scenes.narration: In covalent bonding, nonmetal atoms share electron pairs between overlapping orbitals to construct discrete molecules.
scenes.key_takeaway: Covalent bonds involve localized sharing of valence electron pairs.

scenes.title: Physical Properties in Contrast
scenes.narration: Consequently, ionic salts have very high melting points, while covalent compounds form flexible liquids and gases.
scenes.key_takeaway: Ionic compounds are hard, high-melting crystals; covalent substances form diverse molecules.
